question: Why is the magnetic field at a point on the axial line of a bar magnet generally stronger than at a point at the same distance on the equatorial line?

options.A: Because the axial field is the sum of fields from both poles, while the equatorial field is the difference.
options.B: Because the equatorial field falls off as $1/r^2$ while axial falls off as $1/r^3$.
options.C: Because on the axial line, the point is closer to one pole which dominates, and the fields add up (vectorially) more effectively.
options.D: Because the equatorial line has no magnetic field lines passing through it.
